justification_quote: 'The unreliable transmission of synaptic vesicles in biological neurons is a well studied phenomenon [Katz, 1966; Branco and Staras, 2009], and many studies suggested it as a major source of stochasticity in the brain' (Sec 1, p.2); review by citation.

'we compute the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between an exact restricted Boltzmann distribution and the distribution sampled by a S2M' (Sec 2.1, Fig 2, p.6); sampled distribution matches the RBM Gibbs-sampling reference at this network size.

Table 1 (p.13): spiking S2M 4.4 percent vs RBM 5.0 percent vs previous deterministic-synapse neural sampling eCD 8.1 percent; 'The S2M model is identical to the RBM except that it consists of threshold units with stochastic blank-out synapses with probability 50 percent' (Sec 2.3, p.10); pruning/precision ablations Fig 9.

MNIST generative learning plus pattern completion (Fig 6), sparsity analysis (Fig 7) and pruning/precision robustness (Sec 3.3); 'its performance may generalize to other problems and datasets' (Sec 4, p.19) is speculative.

'The spiking neuron-based synaptic sampling machines outperform existing spike-based unsupervised learners, while potentially offering substantial advantages in terms of power and complexity' (Abstract, p.1); Table 1: 4.4 percent vs Diehl & Cook 5 percent with a much smaller network.

'FearNet is heavily inspired by the dual-memory model of mammalian memory (McClelland et al., 1995), which has considerable experimental support from neuroscience (Frankland et al., 2004; ...; Kitamura et al., 2017)' (Sec 3, p.4); literature review only.

'three brain-inspired modules based on 1) mPFC (long-term storage), 2) HC (recent storage), and 3) BLA for determining whether to use mPFC or HC for recall' (Fig 1, p.2); 'FearNet follows the memory consolidation theory proposed by Kitamura et al. (2017)' (Sec 3, p.4).

Table 2 (p.8): FearNet best Omega-base and Omega-all on all three datasets vs five baselines (1-NN, GeppNet variants, FEL, iCaRL); no ablation removes the dual-memory structure itself (ablations vary sleep frequency Fig 5, covariance Table 6, base-knowledge size).
CIFAR-100, CUB-200, AudioSet (two modalities, Table 1), multi-modal incremental learning (Table 4), base-knowledge size scaling (Sec 6.2), and memory extrapolation to 1,000 classes (Table 5).

'FearNet achieves state-of-the-art performance at incremental class learning on image (CIFAR-100, CUB-200) and audio classification (AudioSet) benchmarks' without storing examples (Abstract, p.1); Tables 2 and 5 support both claims.

'neural models of attention control are largely based on Biased Competition Theory (Desimone & Duncan, 1995)... [PPC] long believed to be responsible for the spatial prioritization' (Introduction, pp.1-2); citation-based.

'ATTNet consists of three interacting components: (1) early parallel visual processing (2) ventral processing, and (3) dorsal processing' with VGG16 conv layers grossly approximating V1-V4 and PPC layers building the priority map (Methods, pp.1-2).

'Model behavior was tested against the fixations made by subjects searching images for the same cued category... while not as strong as the subjects, ATTNet shows guidance to the target by preferentially fixating the target in earlier eye-movements' (Results, Fig 1e-f, p.3).
'trained... to respond target present or target absent for a microwave target... in 2000 kitchen scenes' with '30 subjects... in 80 images' (Methods, p.3); one target category, one dataset.

'ATTNet learned to shift its attention to the visual features of a target category... Both subjects and ATTNet showed evidence for attention being preferentially directed to target goals' (Abstract, p.1); Fig 1f shows exactly this.
'much evidence suggests that the neuromodulator known as dopamine provides basal ganglia target structures with phasic signals that convey a reward prediction error' [3] (Sec I, p.1); citation only.

'we trained the driving agent using a brain-inspired trial-and-error technique, which was in line with the real world situation' (Abstract, p.1); DRQN replaces the last fully connected layer with LSTM (Sec II-B, p.2).
Table I (p.7): Our model 98.33/166/213 vs Stanford supervised 97.46/129.09+1DNF/138.37+2DNF vs Human 94.07/125.30/129.50 (Farm/Raceway/Mountain race times).
'The model was trained using three different tracks... An individual sets of weights was trained separately for each model because each track has different terrain textures' (Sec III, p.5).

'After training for several episodes, the resulting driving agent performed advanced behaviors in the given scene' (Abstract, p.1); consistent with the reward curves (Fig 4) and qualitative descriptions.

'the human brain is capable of not only combining model-free and model-based RL [4] but also adaptively choosing one strategy over the other depending on the context changes [11, 23]... guided by a part of the lateral prefrontal cortex' (Sec 1, p.2); citation-based.

Reliability test: 'latent behavior profile recoverability' comparing model-simulated and human profiles; 'PM-pfcRL2 R=0.302 p=0.006 / R=0.344 p=0.002' while 'all the other models failed to replicate the effect' (Fig 3B, p.5-6).

'we ran large-scale simulations with 10 different Markov decision tasks' (4,920 simulations): 'PM-pfcRL2 successfully solved nine tasks out of ten' and reliability 'effect size... more than three times larger than... all the other models' (Figs 3C, 5, pp.5-7).

'To empirically test the ability to generalize what these models learned... we situated them in the context of environmental volatility' with 10 tasks systematically varying structure (ladder/tree) and uncertainty (fixed/drift/switch/drift+switch) (Sec 4.1, Fig 4, p.6).

'the prefrontal RL reliably encodes the information of high-level policy that humans learned, and this model can generalize the learned policy to a wide range of tasks' (Abstract, p.1); Figs 3 and 5 support both parts.

'Inspired by the human neocortex, HTMs learn and adapt continuously and are robust to noise' and 'emulate the interactions between pyramidal neurons in the neocortex' (Sec I, p.1); HTM theory from Hawkins & Blakeslee [4] and Hawkins & Ahmad [29].

Fig 1 (p.4): 'proximal (feed-forward), apical (feedback), and distal (lateral) dendrites... modeled in HTM neurons as feed-forward, feedback, and lateral connections'; Sec III-A defines encoder, spatial pooler, prediction and temporal pooling (Eqs 1-3, pp.3-4).

Table I (bearings, p.7): TM-HTM+HD 67.05/73.33/56.57 best on Standard and Low FN among 13 baselines including LSTM (33.99) trained 1000+ epochs; Table II (3D printer, p.8): HTM+HD best on Low FN (73.18) while LSTM wins Standard (64.76 vs 63.03).

Two applications: real-world bearing failure data and 3D printer vibration with synthesized anomalies; authors state 'whether HTM's performance on synthetic anomalies translates to real-world PM remains an open research problem' (Sec V-D, p.9).

'our approach outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms at preemptively detecting real-world cases of bearing failures and simulated 3D printer failures... average score of 64.71, surpassing state-of-the-art deep-learning (49.38) and statistical (61.06) methods' (Abstract, p.1).

'humans have a strong generalisation ability which is beneficial from the structural and functional asymmetry of the two sides of the brain' (Abstract, p.1); support is neuroimaging citations [12][13] only, no own evidence.
'the design of dual NCP architectures replicates the human brain left and right hemispheres' (Sec 1 contribution 1, p.2); hemispheres differ only in inter/command neuron counts (Fig 3c, p.5).
'The brain-inspired architecture (CNN-DNCP v4) is 5.80 percent and 34.05 percent more effective than the CNN model with regard to MSE on the cloudy and night time comma.ai recordings' (Sec 4.3, p.7).

Generalisation gain replicated across three domain shifts in two datasets: Udacity lakeside-to-jungle, comma.ai sunny-to-cloudy and sunny-to-night (Fig 5a-c, p.7), with the CNN baseline carried into all three.
'our brain-inspired method outperforms existing methods regarding generalisation when dealing with unseen data' (Abstract, p.1); Fig 5 shows exactly this vs the reference CNN on unseen domains.

'Spiking Neural Network (SNN) is the most famous brain-inspired neural network... Leaky Integrate and Fire (LIF) neurons in SNNs are used to communicate between different time steps' (Abstract, p.1); citation only.

'Different from the accumulation on the time domain in the traditional LIF neurons, we accumulate and fire on the spatial domain instead... we replace the output 1 with u, so the full-precision information is reserved' (Sec 3.2, p.4).
Table 5 ablation (Sec 4.4, p.7): AS-MLP-T 81.3 percent; +dwconv 81.56; +dwconv+AxialShift 81.66; +dwconv+FP-LIF 81.87; Table 8: alternative LIF placements (add LIF 81.38, sub GELU 81.21) worse.

'Experiments on classification, detection and segmentation tasks' (Sec 4): ImageNet (Table 1), COCO Mask/Cascade R-CNN (Table 2), ADE20K UperNet (Table 3), three model scales, AS-MLP baseline at matched params/FLOPs throughout.

'achieves 81.9 percent, 83.3 percent and 83.5 percent top-1 accuracy on ImageNet dataset with only 4.4G, 8.5G and 15.2G FLOPs... state-of-the-art results as far as we know' (Abstract, p.1); Table 1 confirms all numbers.

'FE and FbI are related to multisensory fusion [21] and enhancing the signal-to-noise ratio [20]. FI helps the network maintain a balance... LI plays a role in amplifying the perception... MI is linked to the rhythmic activity' (Sec III-B, p.4); citation only.

'Common neural circuit motifs found in the human brain are Feedforward Excitation (FE), Feedforward Inhibition (FI), Feedback Inhibition (FbI), Lateral Inhibition (LI) and Mutual Inhibition (MI)... We implement them with spiking neurons as shown in Fig. 2b' (Sec III-B, p.4).

'Except for the variables mentioned in the ablation experiments, the parameters and process of the evolutionary algorithm are kept constant' (Sec IV-B, p.7): EB-NAS vs five single-motif models (Fig 4a, +0.88 to +2.15 percent) and vs hierarchical CL-0 (Fig 5, +2.35/+2.54/+1.58/+3.17 percent).

'Extensive experiments on static datasets (CIFAR10, CIFAR100) and neuromorphic datasets (CIFAR10-DVS, DVS128-Gesture) demonstrate that our proposed model boosts energy efficiency' (Abstract); Tables III-V plus ablations on all four datasets.
Abstract names exactly the four evaluated datasets and claims consistent performance and energy-efficiency boosts (p.1); Tables III-V support accuracy, shortest timesteps and lower spike counts.

'Hebbian learning processes can take advantage of the heterogeneity of neural dynamics to strengthen and select the most suitable neural pathways for robust learning and improved task performance [1], [2]' (Sec I, p.1); citation only.

'This proves that the Vth bias tuning matches our expectation' after threshold/leak/feedback tuning experiments (Fig 2, Sec II-C-E, pp.4-5); second circuit 'can be tuned to output three spiking patterns, including chattering behaviors' matching biological pattern classes (Fig 5, Sec II-F, p.5).

'The PSNN consisting of the optoelectronic spiking neuron and an MZI mesh synaptic network achieves 89.3 percent accuracy on the Iris dataset' (Abstract / Sec III-B, p.7); no homogeneous-neuron control or accuracy-vs-heterogeneity ablation.
Single-layer PSNN on the 150-sample Iris dataset with offline-trained weights (Sec III-B, p.7); no other tasks, datasets or scales.

Abstract claims are demonstration-scoped: 'programmed to tune four essential parameters', 'three spiking patterns', '89.3 percent accuracy on the Iris dataset', and 36.84 fJ/spike explicitly labeled 'predicted' for ASAP7 (p.1).
'brain-inspired NN architectures prioritize it [locality], leading to modularity... tend to exhibit high sparsity' (Sec 1, p.2); biological rationale is citation-only ([4][13][15][16]).

'BIMT incorporates the notion of geometry and distance... by associating a coordinate with each neural unit' (Sec 3, p.5); L1 sparsity, distance penalty and unit swapping implemented in PyTorch (Sec 3.1).
'modular PINN has a test error (calculated as MSE) that is approximately two orders lower than the fully-connected MLP PINN' with 9 vs 9 neural units; Euclidean error 0.083 vs 0.57 (Fig 5, p.9).

'this study represents only an initial exploration... focused primarily on simple one-dimensional problems and utilized only a single building block' (Sec 6, p.11); spectral-bias trend shown across source-term frequencies (Fig 4, p.8).

Abstract claims bare-minimum architectures ('often consisting of a few neural units'), spectral-bias manifestation, and modular PINN outperforming equal-size fully connected MLPs (p.1); each is shown in Figs 2-5.

'Biological evidence shows that reward-related neurotransmitters can control the process of myelination and demyelination [23]' (Sec 2.1, p.4); myelination-as-delay-learning and homeostasis claims rest on citations.

RDL Eq (1)-(3), inhibitory-neuron rules, intervallic homeostasis Eq (4), threshold adaptation Eq (5), decision homeostasis Eq (6) implement the cited mechanisms on LIF neurons (Secs 2.1-2.7, pp.4-10).

Sec 3.5 mechanism-by-mechanism ablations: decentralization -7.39 percent test accuracy, decision homeostasis -3.68 percent, threshold adaptation -3.16 percent, homeostasis -2.1 percent, inhibitory rules -1.58 percent, RDL delays -3.15 (fixed) / -3.68 (random) percent (pp.16-24).
'we employ the DVS128-Gesture dataset [27] as our benchmark' (Sec 3.1, p.11); no second dataset, task, or scale anywhere in the paper.
'our model outperforms previous biologically plausible models and competes with deep supervised models' (Abstract, p.1); Table 1: 90.52 vs deep models 97.08/99.58 and supervised SNNs 92.7-95.54.
'Spiking Neural Networks transmit information through spike sequences, which encode both temporal and spatial information' (Sec 1, p.1); LIF dynamics cited from [2], no own biological evidence.

'we use the LIF neuron model for modeling... discretize it to facilitate forward process and training' with surrogate gradient (Sec 3.1, pp.3-4); spiking self-attention 'combines a LIF layer with a multi-head self-attention mechanism' (Sec 3.3, p.5).

'The main difference between them is whether there is Spiking Transformer (ST)' (Sec 4.2, p.7): Table 1 - STMDP 0.754/0.94/0.80/0.540 vs DPT 0.707/0.86/0.72/0.540, vs DIT 0.657/0.92/0.80/0.540, vs SDPT (spiking, no modulation) 0.747/0.22/0.04/0.00.
'four robotic manipulation tasks: PushT, Can, Square and ToolHang' (Sec 4.1, p.6); Table 1 shows mixed results (STMDP-I best only on Square; ToolHang tied).
'Our model consistently outperforms existing Transformer-based diffusion policy method. Especially in Can task, we achieved an improvement of 8 percent' (Abstract, p.1).

'the brain's cross-regional temporal development mechanisms, where the progressive formation, reorganization, and pruning of connections from basic to advanced regions, facilitate knowledge transfer and prevent network redundancy' (Abstract, p.1); developmental facts cited from [2][3][4][17][18].

'the total number of local connections first increases, then decreases, and finally stabilizes. This pattern aligns with the biological brain' (Sec 2.5, Fig 3A, p.9); long-range connections 'gradually increase... in accordance with the temporal developmental patterns' (p.9).

Comparisons vs EWC, MAS, HNET, LSTM NET, DualNet, DSD-SNN, SOR-SNN (Fig 2E: 68.88 percent average, +6.15 percent over second best) and controls vs direct training / direct pruning (Fig 2F-G: arm task 29.9 / 63.02 vs 70.33 percent; button 60->20 after pruning vs 80 percent at higher pruning) and vs no-local-inhibition (Sec 2.4).

'nine tasks spanning three cognitive functions' - visual recognition (sketch/cartoon/photo), motor control (Walker/Reacher), environmental interaction (metaworld) - with accuracy/return/success-rate metrics (Sec 2.1-2.2, Figs 2-3).

'achieve continual learning capabilities while reducing network scale, without introducing regularization, replay, or freezing strategies, and achieving superior accuracy on new tasks compared to direct learning' (Abstract, p.1); Secs 2.3-2.4 show exactly this.

'Physiological studies in recent years have established a causal relationship between heterogeneous dendritic axons and the firing properties of neurons [8]' (Introduction, p.1); cited structures (cortical columns, heterogeneous neurons/dendrites, small-world connectivity) are supported only by citation, no own biological evidence.

'Similar to how cortical columns act as the fundamental functional units of the cerebral cortex, the CC also serves as the basic functional unit in TaiBai' (Sec III-A, p.4); LIF/ALIF/dendrite dynamics implemented via the brain-inspired instruction set (Fig 9, Sec IV-B).

Fig 15 'TaiBai-homogeneous baseline, obtained by deploying SRNN without heterogeneous neurons, DHSFNN without dendrites, and BCI cross-day decoding without on-chip learning' (p.14); headline efficiency is 'more than 200 times' vs RTX 3090 obtained via the chip simulator (Sec V-B-2, Figs 15b-c).

Three applications on the FPGA prototype (ECG QTDB, speech SHD, macaque BCI cross-day) plus three benchmark networks in simulation (Table II, Figs 13-15); efficiency gain persists in direction across task families with honest analysis of firing-rate dependence (p.12, p.14).

Abstract: 'could achieve more than 200 times higher energy efficiency than a standard NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU at a comparable accuracy' (p.1); own benchmark suite reports 'power efficiency improved by 6 to 20 times' (Fig 13d, p.12).

'A key factor that protects humans from drastic forgetting is thought to be the reactivation of neural activity patterns representing previous experiences - referred to as memory replay (Wilson and McNaughton 1994, Rasch and Born 2007...)' (Sec 1, p.1); citation-based.

Appendix B: 'the generator(hippocampus) merged into the main model(cortex)... internal replay replays the representations of previously learned classes at the hidden level, rather than at the input level' because 'the brain does not replay memories down to the input level' (pp.8-9).

'we compare model with internal replay (w/ IR) and model without internal replay (w/o IR)... on BIR and BIR + SI' (Sec 3.1, p.2): Figs 1-2 show IR mitigates forgetting (higher retention ratio, lower forgetting score) at the cost of lower initial accuracy.
'We train and test on CIFAR-100 in class-IL scenario' only (Sec 3.1, pp.2-3); no second dataset or task in this paper.

'internal replay significantly mitigates forgetting, especially when paired with SI, but at the cost of reduced initial task accuracy, highlighting a trade-off... These results underscore the limitations of current brain-inspired methods' (Abstract, p.1); Figs 1-3 show exactly this.

'The neural basis of Path Integration (PI) mechanism [2] provides crucial guidance for navigation tasks, such as Dead Reckoning (DR) and SLAM' (Sec I, p.1); HDC/GC structure-computation link is citation-based ([2][18]).

'benchmark evaluations... to verify the representational fidelity of this AI-replicated neurodynamics' (Sec I, p.2): Figs 6-7 show ANN-fitted decoding does not deviate significantly from CANN over 4,800+ frames with abrupt changes; bump dynamics reproduce CANN wrap-around continuity (Figs 8-9, pp.9-11).

Table I (p.9): This work 721.6s @PC / 756.1s @Edge with MAE 2.5 / RMSE 2.9 / MTE 5.9, identical accuracy to NeuroSLAM (871.4s / 1478.1s) and far better than pure VO (7.0/7.5/12.3); +17.5 percent PC, +48.9 percent edge efficiency.

Two datasets (NeuroSLAM garage + self-built corridor), two platforms (RTX 4060 PC + Raspberry Pi 4B), three network resolutions (25/75, 37/111, 49/147) with identical trajectory accuracy and ~2 percent runtime variation (Sec IV-C, p.9).
'approximately 17.5 percent improvement on general-purpose computing platforms and 40-50 percent on edge devices' while 'enhancing the practicality of BIN technology' (Abstract, p.1).

'biological neural systems... leverage mechanisms such as selective neuroplasticity [7, 8], attentional modulation [9], and progressive learning [10]' (Sec 1, p.2); the cited references are weakly related (e.g. [9] is an ADHD screening ML study).

'we introduce Focal Loss as a brain-inspired attention modulation mechanism' (Sec 2.3.1, p.4); staged layer freezing framed as selective neural plasticity (Sec 2.5); 'cosine annealing with warm restarts are adopted to mimic rhythmic regulation' (Abstract).
Table 4 (Sec 3.4, p.9): Brain-Inspired Hybrid 85.00 percent / AUC 0.9372 / F1 0.8657 vs ResNet18 76.67/0.8453/0.7821, ResNet34 79.17, quantum-enhanced ResNet18 81.67.
'an independent test set comprising 120 coronary angiography images (60 positive and 60 negative cases)' (Sec 3.2, p.8); single binary task, single dataset, no external validation.

'This study validates the effectiveness of brain-inspired learning mechanisms in lightweight medical image analysis and provides a biologically plausible and deployable solution' (Conclusion, p.1/p.12).
